recipes.name: Slow-Baked Beef Brisket with Gravy
ingredients_raw: 1 teaspoon unseasoned meat tenderizer (such as Adolph's®)
1 (1 ounce) package dry onion soup mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 275 degrees F (135 degrees C). Season beef brisket with garlic salt and meat tenderizer; place in a 9x13-inch baking dish.
Mix beef gravy, Italian salad dressing, mushrooms, and onion soup mix in a bowl. Pour mixture over beef brisket. Cover tightly with aluminum foil.
Bake in the preheated oven until very tender, 4 to 5 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow-Baked Beef Brisket with Gravy
raw_recipe.description: This tender beef brisket, smothered in mushroom gravy, is so easy to make. Everything goes into the baking dish and cooks in the oven, low and slow.

review.reviewBody: I submitted this recipe and just wanted to mention that I do not drain the mushrooms, the juice is needed for the gravy. Enjoy!

I made this tonight with a few minor adjustments. I used garlic instead of garlic salt and seasoned salt in place on meat tenderizer. And I did not have beef gravy, so I just add water to the italian dressing. mushroom , and dry onion soup mix. It was so tender. Probably the best brisket I have made in a long time. I cooked for 3 hrs 45 mins... 
Served it mashed potatoes and gravy from the meat.

Totally easy. Melt-in-your-mouth! The Brisket came out wonderful! I was out of garlic powder & simply used salt. The onion soup mix was the key. I also substituted the beef gravy for beef broth with a dash of Gravy master. (but a can of onion soup, or beef broth with chopped onions will do just fine as well!) The Italian salad dressing is important. Make some of it if you have to. (Oil, vinegar, & your favorite Italian spices) As long as the meat is lightly seasoned, and sitting 1/3 deep in whatever liquid you concoct... having it tightly covered in foil will make it come out fine! Be creative & use what you have in the pantry. 275 degrees for 4 hours. Pair with any starch, vegetable & wine! Enjoy!

I’m going to be honest. This is not something I’d normally make. I usually make everything from scratch and don’t normally use canned/jarred/premade ingredients. But I’m injured and needed something super easy. This was actually amazing and I’m going to keep in rotation. I made exactly as written but skimmed fat off and reduced gravy on stovetop at the end.

Very easy recipe to follow. I had to improvise the onion soup mix with an Allrecipes onion soup recipe. 

The leftovers made great BBQ Brisket sandwiches. 

I will use the recipe again.

I was curious about using a slow cooker, but I also couldn’t find beef brisket at the store. So I ended up using a corned beef brisket, knowing it’s not the same thing. First, it took longer to cook. I don’t know if it was the corned beef or the slow cooker or both, but it really needed to cook at least 8 hours on high or 10-12 hours on low. The other issue was how salty it was. The corned beef is saltier than regular beef brisket, but the gravy was super salty. I ended up just making a brown gravy to serve with the beef rather than using the cooking gravy. I considered adding a bunch of water and cornstarch, but it would have made way more gravy than we needed. I did use a bit of the cooking gravy in the brown gravy, but most of it went down the drain. I realize I didn’t follow the directions but I have to rate this 3 stars for the salt and having to waste it. And it would have been helpful to include slow cooker directions along with the oven directions.

Absolutely delicious!! I have never made a brisket before so I was nervous. I cooked it exactly like the recipe said and cooked it for five hours. It was tender and very tasty. Very easy to put together too! I wouldn't change a thing!
So easy, so good! Had a just under three pound piece...the mix of Italian dressing and onion soup ...mmm...let it sit in the oven for an extra hour...will definitely make again!!!
Wonderfully tender and flavorful brisket! Followed recipe as written and will make again.
Very good. Husband especially loved it! In fact he wants this for Christmas dinner instead of our usual prime rib.
Wonderful, easy recipe. Tiny bit too salty, but that can be adjusted next time. We will make it again.

very nice use for brisket, turned out very flavorful,
was easy to make, just put it in the oven and forget it.
the only change i made was to cut back on the salt, by about half. i had it with mashed potatoes and a spinach, water melon salad, from this site. made a great meal. will make again.
